questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. His research on the migratory patterns of the birds is run-of-the-mill.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

His research on the migratory patterns of the birds is run-of-the-mill.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4)

Key Points

  • The word "run-of-the-mill" means something that is ordinary and not special or exciting in any way. (साधारण)
    • Example: The movie was just a run-of-the-mill thriller, nothing extraordinary.
  • "Average" refers to something that is typical, normal, or usual; not special or exceptional. (औसत)
    • Example: His performance was average, neither outstanding nor poor.

Therefore, the correct meaning of the given idiom is 'average.'

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Absurd (बेतुका): Something that is ridiculous or unreasonable.
    • Example: The idea of flying pigs is completely absurd.
  • One in a million (लाखों में एक): Something that is very special or unique.
    • Example: Her talent is truly one in a million.
  • Trash (कचरा): Something that is of very poor quality.
    • Example: The novel was so bad it was just trash.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Like a bat out of hell
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Like a bat out of hell
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Like a bat out of hell" means to move very fast and wildly. (बहुत तेज और बेकाबू तरीके से)
    • Example: He ran out of the room like a bat out of hell when he heard the fire alarm.
  • Very fast and wildly indicates a rapid and uncontrolled manner. (बहुत तेज और बेकाबू तरीके से)
    • Example: The motorcycle sped down the highway very fast and wildly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings:

  • In a bad situation (खराब स्थिति में): Facing or experiencing difficulties.
    • Example: He found himself in a bad situation after losing his job.
  • Defeated (पराजित): Having been beaten in a battle or other contest.
    • Example: The team felt defeated after losing the final match.
  • Impossible (असंभव): Not able to occur, exist, or be done.
    • Example: It seems impossible to complete this project within the deadline.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Run errands

Run errands

options.text: To go out to buy or do something
options.html: To go out to buy or do something

options.text: To participate in a race through unfair means

options.text: To finish running before the end point

options.text: To do something incorrectly or erroneous in haste

The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Run errands" means to go out to buy or do something. (काम के लिए बाहर जाना)
    • Example: She spent the afternoon running errands, including picking up groceries and mailing a package.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 2: To participate in a race through unfair means (अनुचित साधनों से दौड़ में भाग लेना):

Question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Run errands

questions.question: Based on the situation in the given sentence, select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment. There are several people who find themselves a dominating person in a group .
questions.questionHtml:
Based on the situation in the given sentence, select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment.
There are several people who find themselves a dominating person in a group.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cock of the walk.

Key Points

  • The idiom "A bone of contention" means something that is a cause of argument or disagreement. (विवाद का कारण)
    • Example: The boundary line between the two properties has always been a bone of contention.
  • The phrase "A man of his words" refers to someone who keeps promises and is reliable. (अपने शब्दों का पक्का व्यक्ति)
    • Example: John is a man of his words; he always does what he says he will.
  • The idiom "Cock of the walk" means a person who acts as if they are the most important in a group. (गुरूर में रहने वाला व्यक्ति)
    • Example: Ever since his promotion, he's been strutting around the office like the cock of the walk.
  • The phrase "A white elephant" refers to something that has cost a lot of money but has no useful purpose. (बहुत खर्चीली पर अनुपयोगी चीज)
    • Example: The new stadium is a white elephant. It cost a fortune but is rarely used.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Cock of the walk.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • A bone of contention (विवाद का कारण): Something that people argue about.
    • Example: The distribution of the property became a bone of contention among the family members.
  • A man of his words (अपने शब्दों का पक्का व्यक्ति): Someone who is reliable and keeps promises.
    • Example: Everyone respects him because he is a man of his words.
  • A white elephant (बहुत खर्चीली पर अनुपयोगी चीज): An expensive item that is difficult to maintain and is more trouble than it is worth.
    • Example: The old mansion turned out to be a white elephant for the new owners.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom: 'Hold someone's feet to the fire'
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom:
'Hold someone's feet to the fire'

options.text: Agree upon a shared venture with full conviction
options.html: Agree upon a shared venture with full conviction

options.text: Take big risks without knowing the consequences
options.html: Take big risks without knowing the consequences

options.text: Insist that someone fulfill their promises or obligations
options.html: Insist that someone fulfill their promises or obligations

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Insist that someone fulfill their promises or obligations.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Hold someone's feet to the fire" means to put pressure on someone to ensure they fulfill their promises, duties, or obligations. (किसी पर दबाव बनाना ताकि वह अपना वादा या जिम्मेदारी निभाए।)
    • Example: The manager held the team's feet to the fire to ensure the project was completed on time.
  • Explanation of the correct answer: The idiom emphasises accountability and persistence in ensuring that someone delivers what they committed to.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Out of spirits
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Out of spirits
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Gloomy.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Out of spirits" refers to someone feeling sad, down, or discouraged. (उदास)
    • Example: After losing the match, he was out of spirits and needed some cheering up.
  • "Gloomy" means feeling downhearted, sad, or depressed. (निराशाजनक)
    • Example: The gloomy weather matched her mood after hearing the bad news.
  • Hence, the idiom "Out of spirits" is best represented by the word "Gloomy."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Cheerful (हंसमुख): Feeling or showing happiness and optimism.
    • Example: Despite the challenges, she remained cheerful and kept everyone motivated.
  • Hurt (चोट पहुंचाना): Feeling emotional pain or physical injury.
    • Example: He was hurt by the harsh words of his friend.
  • Obsolete (पुराना): No longer in use or outdated.
    • Example: The typewriter has become obsolete in the age of computers.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Grease someone's palm
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Grease someone's palm
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. "To bribe someone".

Key Points

  • The idiom "Grease someone's palm" means to bribe someone in order to gain favor or secure a benefit. (किसी को रिश्वत देना)
    • Example: He had to grease the officer's palm to get his work done quickly.
  • "Bribe" refers to giving someone money or something valuable to persuade them to act dishonestly in your favor. (रिश्वत देना)
    • Example: The contractor attempted to bribe the official to approve the faulty construction project.
  • Hence, the idiom "Grease someone's palm" directly refers to the act of bribing someone.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: To flatter someone (किसी की चापलूसी करना): To excessively praise or compliment someone, often to gain favor.
    • Example: She tried to flatter her boss to get a promotion.
  • Option 2: To beat someone (किसी को मारना): To physically attack or defeat someone.
    • Example: The team managed to beat their rivals in the final match.
  • Option 3: To abuse someone (किसी का अपमान करना): To mistreat or speak rudely to someone.
    • Example: The teacher warned the students not to abuse each other during the debate.

questions.question: Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. His remarks made the matter worse.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.
His remarks made the matter worse.

options.text: Killed two birds with one stone
options.html: Killed two birds with one stone

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Added fuel to the fire.

Key Points

  • The phrase "Added fuel to the fire" means to make a bad situation worse by doing or saying something that causes more anger or difficulty. (आग में घी डालना)
    • Example: Instead of calming the argument, his sarcastic comment only added fuel to the fire.
  • The sentence "His remarks made the matter worse" implies that his remarks intensified the problem, which perfectly aligns with the idiom "added fuel to the fire." (आग में घी डालने जैसा काम किया।)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Added fuel to the fire.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Spilled the beans (राज खोल देना): To reveal a secret or confidential information unintentionally or intentionally.
    • Example: She accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party.
  • Made a splash (धूम मचाना): To attract a lot of attention or make a big impression.
    • Example: The new fashion designer made a splash with her innovative designs.
  • Killed two birds with one stone (एक तीर से दो निशाने): To accomplish two objectives with a single action.
    • Example: By attending the conference, he killed two birds with one stone: he networked with professionals and learned new skills.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Get down to brass tacks
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Get down to brass tacks
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1'.

Key Points

  • The idiom "get down to brass tacks" means to start to consider the basic, essential, or important details of a job or task, to focus on the most important details.
  • "To become serious about something" - This phrase generally implies that someone is beginning to focus or concentrate on something, or has decided to take something seriously.

Therefore, the correct answer is: 'To become serious about something'.

Additional Information

  • Explanation for other options:
    • "Get fired from the job" - This means that someone has been dismissed or let go from their job, typically because of poor performance or some violation of company policy. It doesn't relate to the idiom "get down to brass tacks."
    • "Compromise, cooperation between people" - This indicates a state of agreement reached by adjustment of conflicting or opposing claims, principles, etc., by mutual concessions. It does not encapsulate the meaning of "get down to brass tacks," which pertains to dealing with important details rather than resolving disputes.
    • "To be ready" - This generally means to be prepared for an event or situation. While it may be related in some contexts (you need to be ready before getting down to brass tacks), it doesn't convey the specific idea of dealing with the basic or most important aspects of a situation.

questions.question: In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom Phrase. A blind spot
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom Phrase.

A blind spot

options.text: A person with no emotional feelings
options.html: A person with no emotional feelings

options.text: A situation where no progress is made
options.html: A situation where no progress is made

options.text: An area in your range of vision that you cannot see properly
options.html: An area in your range of vision that you cannot see properly

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 4'.

Key Points

  • The idiom "a blind spot" refers to an area in one's range of vision that cannot be seen properly.(किसी की दृष्टि की सीमा का वह क्षेत्र जिसे ठीक से नहीं देखा जा सकता)
  • It can also metaphorically refer to an area of knowledge or understanding where one is lacking or has difficulty comprehending.(यह रूपक रूप से ज्ञान या समझ के उस क्षेत्र को भी संदर्भित कर सकता है जहां किसी के पास कमी है या उसे समझने में कठिनाई हो रही है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: 'An area in your range of vision that you cannot see properly.'

Additional Information

  • "A person who is blind" is a literal description and doesn't capture the idiomatic meaning of a "blind spot".(यह एक शाब्दिक वर्णन है और इसमें "ब्लाइंड स्पॉट" का मुहावरेदार अर्थ शामिल नहीं है)
  • "A person with no emotional feelings" does not align with the meaning of "blind spot".("ब्लाइंड स्पॉट" के अर्थ से मेल नहीं खाता)
  • "A situation where no progress is made" is also not a direct interpretation of the idiom.(यह भी मुहावरे की सीधी व्याख्या नहीं है)

questions.question: In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase. To meet one's eyes
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

options.text: To look at someone directly while they are looking at you

  • When you "meet someone's eyes," you are looking directly into their eyes while they are looking back into yours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: 'To look at someone directly while they are looking at you'.

questions.question: In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom Phrase. In the long run
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom Phrase.

In the long run
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "In the end".

Key Points

  • The idiom "in the long run" refers to what will happen over time or eventually, despite any delays or complications that may arise in the short term.
  • "In the end": This is the correct choice. Both "in the end" and "in the long run" refer to final outcomes. They imply that, despite what happens in the immediate future or any difficulties we may encounter, a certain result will eventually manifest.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 4".

Additional Information

  • "Lack of energy": This does not relate to the idiom "in the long run". Rather, it is an idiom itself that refers to feeling tired or drained. There's no inherent implication of a timeline or eventual outcome in this phrase.
  • "Long walk": This is a literal phrase referring to a lengthy physical journey. While it certainly involves the passage of time, it does not communicate the same concept as "in the long run", which refers to a final outcome or consequence that arises over time.
  • "In tough times": This phrase refers to challenging periods in life. While it involves a duration of time like "in the long run", it doesn't imply an eventual outcome or consequences over time. Instead, it refers to enduring hardship in the present or near future.

questions.solution: "To be at a crossroads" is an idiomatic expression that means to be at a point in one's life or a situation where a decision or choice between two or more options is imminent. It suggests a critical moment where one must choose a path or make a significant decision that will shape the future. Being at a crossroads implies uncertainty about which direction to take and the need to make a crucial choice. Example: After completing his degree, John found himself at a crossroads in his career.

questions.question: Direction: In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase. To get under one's skin
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To get under one's skin
questions.solution: The words "anger" and "irritate" both describe actions that cause negative emotions, but they differ in intensity and duration. "Anger" is a strong emotion involving a sense of displeasure or hostility. It often arises in response to a perceived injustice, wrongdoing, or frustration. "Irritate" refers to the act of provoking mild annoyance or provoking a slight feeling of discomfort. It is generally less intense than anger and may result from minor annoyances.

A broth of a boy
questions.solution: The idiom "a broth of a boy" is used to describe a young person who is full of energy and enthusiasm. Example: It's hard to imagine just by looking at him that this tousle-haired broth of a boy could be one of the greatest scientific minds in the country. The word "broth" in this context means a mixture or combination of different qualities. This idiom is typically used in a positive way to describe someone who is lively and fun to be around.

questions.solution: The expression "long in the tooth" is an idiom that is often used to describe someone who is old or aging. Example: Even though he's a seasoned programmer, some might say he's getting a bit long in the tooth in the rapidly evolving tech industry. It's a figurative way of referring to the fact that as horses age, their gums recede, making their teeth appear longer. Therefore, when someone says another person is "long in the tooth," they are suggesting that the individual is getting older.
